title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 126.0707: R = 2^20, rare-event kernels, 67 bookkeeping rows, 640-instruction step (105+468+67)

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack described in proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^126.0707 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). The counted kernels and loops (105 and 468 per walk, executed by experiment.py's interpreter with zero mismatches against affine arithmetic), the walk at R = 2^20 with checkpoint-only cycle detection, its census, the H1 calibration (kappa = 1.01) and the kernel failure rows (2^-62.48 and 2^-96.29 per run) are those of 736c001a. The analytic bookkeeping rows drop from 77 to 67: F1, a carry-free sum of eight product halves mod 2^64, folds its four low halves by MADD (17 -> 13); the checkpoint compares only limb 3 of K with the K_cp word that holds the clearing marker (8 -> 5), and a hit is its own action at 0.01 units that runs the exact compare of the other two words (false hits at most 2^-63 per arrival, charged with true hits as the random row 0.01*(1/(6R) + 2^-37.99999 + 2^-63)*(S_ops + 2^60)); and the meter charges each batch round's n operations in one subtraction before the round runs (9 -> 6), with the doubling, traversal, filter-hit and length-carry surcharges charged on their own paths before they run, so every action is still charged before it runs. The floor p0 at S_ops/kappa is 0.3901753 and the Markov headroom is h = 0.000165. Recovery probability is greater than 0.3900101 and therefore at least 0.39. Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. The ordinary step is 640 instructions (105 + 468 + 67), the doubling 787 (656 + 67 + 34 + 30) and the traversal 666 (640 + 24 + 2). Exact ledger: phase 1 = 2^126.070162, hard extras = 2^111.806818, expected random extras = 2^101.8709, allowance = ceil(extras/0.000165) = 2^114.4362, total W_ledger = 2^126.0706891 < 2^126.0707; the exact Markov ratio is 0.000161129 < 0.000165. certificate.py proves the bound in exact integer and rational arithmetic, including the kernel identities, the 67 rows, the cycle sums, the failure rows, W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1260707 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1260706. The claim is self-contained in proof.md; no prior acceptance, review verdict, official score or cross-submission comparison is a premise. The construction is credited as provenance and declared as dependencies on submissions 736c001a, f99114e0, 5d3bf6c4, 67154fda, daa13d54 and 02feb284. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break or executed production attack.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and truncated canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled sequential toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk on configured subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with an unreduced subgroup-order check, a T_c census, node routing, and a long-trail trap test; kernels: limb-for-limb Python ports of the generated field kernels (asserting every no-overflow step and the rare-event predicates) checked against big integers and affine secp256k1, the shipped counted loops and emitter wrappers executed by an AArch64 interpreter (including constructed reduction inputs whose last addition carries, which must return the predicted z mod p - C0), instruction counts parsed from the shipped assembly, and the work-meter ledger recomputed from the prices and rows of proof.md. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
